title: When THE CONNOISSEUR meets THE SURGEON:
subtitle: The Decay of the Aura

script.text: In the flicker of a projection booth, two figures watch the reels spin. The film is Battleship Potemkin.
One figure is THE CONNOISSEUR (representing Cult Value/Traditional Aesthetics). He wears velvet and mourns the loss of the unique object.

script.speaker: THE Connoisseur
script.text: Look at this

script.speaker: THE Connoisseur
script.text: This has Aura. It is unique. It has a history. It was touched by the artist, then by the priest, then by the collector. It has a presence in time and space. It demands contemplation. You must stand before it in silence
The other figure is THE SURGEON (representing Exhibition Value/The Camera). He wears a lab coat and holds a scalpel (or a lens). He does not contemplate; he penetrates.

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: Your Aura is a distance

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: It is the authority of the object. But the masses do not want distance. They want closeness. They want to pry the object from its shell. They want to consume it
The Surgeon points to the screen, where a montage of machinery and faces flashes by at 24 frames per second.

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: The camera does not respect the whole

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: It cuts. It isolates. It zooms in. It reveals the "optical unconscious"—the slow motion of a horse, the micro-expression of a face. It destroys the Aura, but it democratizes the image. The painting had one viewer; the film has millions
The Connoisseur shudders.

script.speaker: THE CONNOISSEUR
script.text: It is distraction! The masses absorb the art, instead of being absorbed by it. They are like a critic who is also absent-minded. There is no ritual left. Only politics

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: Precisely

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: When the criterion of authenticity ceases to apply, the function of art is reversed. Instead of being based on ritual, it is based on politics
He gestures to the newsreel playing before the feature. It shows a massive military parade.

script.speaker: THE NEWSREEL
script.text: Fascism attempts to organize the masses without changing property relations
, The Surgeon warns.

script.speaker: THE SURGEON
script.text: It gives them expression, but not rights. It aestheticizes politics. It turns war into a spectacle. It says: Fiat ars—pereat mundus (Let art be created, though the world perish)
The Connoisseur looks at the screen, mesmerized by the beauty of the destruction.

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: We must respond

script.speaker: THE Surgeon
script.text: Communism responds by politicizing art. We do not need the Aura. We need the Shock. We need an art that hits the spectator like a bullet
